candidates.name: Compiz Web
candidates.description: Shader-driven page navigation transitions inspired by the Compiz Linux window manager: each navigation runs a WebGL fragment shader that reads the leaving and entering pages as live textures via the experimental texElementImage2D() API and composites them through switchable effects (cube spins, flips). Falls back to plain page swaps in unsupported browsers.
candidates.creator: Max Leiter
techniques: per-effect shader modules with uniforms and timing

licensing.notes: GitHub repo fetched; licence file not inspected.

candidates.research_notes: Fetched the GitHub page and read the README embedded in the HTML: documents the exact pipeline (HTML laid out but not painted, rendered to WebGL textures, blended by fragment shader). Experimental HTML-in-Canvas requirement (Chrome Canary flag) limits portability today, but it is the most direct hint of where DOM-texture page transitions are heading; highly reusable as a design reference even without the novel API.
candidates.otxyn_potential: High as a future-facing pattern: 'shader composites the whole page pair' transitions; could be re-implemented today with html-to-image rasterization + WebGL texture blending.

candidates.name: Custom Page Transitions in Astro with Barba.js and GSAP
candidates.description: A multi-technique page-transition system: Barba.js intercepts navigation and preloads the next page, then GSAP plays a sequence of expressive leave/enter effects including a WebGL noise-reveal overlay, SVG morphing, overlay panels and animated pseudo-elements, scoped per-route via Barba rules.
candidates.creator: Iqbal Muthahhary

licensing.notes: Tutorial free to read; repo licence not inspected.

candidates.research_notes: Fetched the article HTML (excerpt returned real content: Barba.js lifecycle hooks, WebGLPageTransition class with a noise pattern reveal inspired by faint-film.com) and the GitHub repo URL appears in the article. Verified both article (HTTP 200) and repo (HTTP 200). A current (April 2026), multi-variant reference covering the main transition families in one codebase.
candidates.otxyn_potential: Very high: acts as a taxonomy for the page-transition category — noise reveal, SVG morph, overlay panels, pseudo-element wipes — each extractable as a standalone pattern.

candidates.name: View Transitions Demos (Bramus / Chrome DevRel)
candidates.description: Official collection of View Transitions API demos: same-document (SPA) and cross-document (MPA) transitions including directional pagination sliding, shared-element morphs, types-based asymmetric transitions, using document.startViewTransition() and CSS animation overrides.
candidates.creator: Bramus Van Damme (Chrome DevRel)

licensing.notes: Demo pages by Google DevRel; reuse terms not stated on the fetched page.

candidates.research_notes: Fetched the index (HTTP 200, real content listing demos with browser-support notes). Native-browser transition machinery — extremely cheap to implement, increasingly supported across Chrome/Safari/Firefox per the page's own notes.
candidates.otxyn_potential: High as the baseline 'standard platform' pattern for the library; every custom page transition should be benchmarked against what View Transitions gives for free.

candidates.name: View Transitions Gallery Demo (vanilla-breeze)
candidates.description: Compact self-contained gallery demo: clicking a card morphs it into a detail view via the View Transitions API, with view-transition-name applied automatically from data-vt-name attributes so shared-element morphing works without manual bookkeeping.
candidates.creator: vanilla-breeze
techniques: automatic view-transition-name assignment from data attributes

licensing.notes: Licence not stated on fetched page.

candidates.research_notes: Fetched page (HTTP 200) — its visible text documents the data-vt-name auto-naming technique. The free-lookup of the same pattern as the Chrome demos, useful as a minimal single-page reference.
candidates.otxyn_potential: Medium: a minimal, dependency-free shared-element morph recipe; good 'smallest possible implementation' entry for the library.

candidates.name: WebGL Distortion Hover Effects
candidates.description: Hover library that transitions between two images in a Three.js plane using a displacement map: RGB distortion of the first image, a fade, then reversed displacement reveals the second image; different displacement textures produce radically different looks.
candidates.creator: Codrops team
techniques: crossfade with displacement ramp for texture A/B swap
configurable displacement textures for many looks

licensing.notes: Codrops resource; typical Codrops free-use-with-credit terms but licence not verified.

candidates.research_notes: Article fetched and excerpt inspected; demo page verified HTTP 200. Classic, hugely-referenced displacement transition; the article documents the exact 3-step algorithm (distort → fade → reverse displace).
candidates.otxyn_potential: High: canonical WebGL image-to-image reveal — one shader covers dozens of brand identities depending on the displacement texture.

candidates.name: Image Reveal Hover Effects
candidates.description: A set of link hover effects where a thumbnail is revealed with different clip/translate/opacity gymnastics (scissor block reveals, SVG clip, first-line/first-letter overlap tricks) inspired by Fuge, Louis Ansa and Zhenya Rynzhuk, animated with TweenMax.
candidates.creator: Codrops (Manoela Ilic)
techniques: dynamic thumbnail follow of the cursor

licensing.notes: Codrops resource; licence not verified.

candidates.research_notes: Demo page and GitHub repo both fetched HTTP 200 (repo URL extracted from the article HTML). Several distinct reveal variants live in one repo — cheap to mine for multiple library entries.
candidates.otxyn_potential: High: DOM/SVG-only alternative to the WebGL reveal family; 'thumbnail that follows link hover' is a staple editorial-site effect.

candidates.name: Revealing Images With CSS Mask Animations
candidates.description: Temani Afif's single-image hover effect using only mask layers: multiple radial/linear gradients combined with mask-composite (add/intersect) create a crosshair-like aperture that shrinks from the corners, with a custom property --k toggling grayscale→color and mask radii — no JavaScript.
candidates.creator: Temani Afif
techniques: hover-toggled custom property driving whole animation

licensing.notes: Article and demo pens live on CodePen; pen code licence not verified. Several demo pen URLs (e.g. codepen.io/smashingmag/pen/abQGGew, wvQOJrZ) were extracted from the article HTML but not individually fetched.

candidates.research_notes: Article fetched (HTTP 200) and the mask-composite/--k technique confirmed in the returned excerpt. Pure-CSS, zero-dependency mask reveal family — the article itself hosts ~5 live variations.
candidates.otxyn_potential: High: the cheapest possible mask-transition primitive; pairs well with wipe patterns as the 'CSS-only tier' of the library.

candidates.name: curtains.js
candidates.description: WebGL library that turns DOM elements into interactive textured planes; its examples include displacement/spherical transitions where a geometry shader 'mask' moves across a plane to swap or distort images, all synced to the real HTML elements.
candidates.creator: Martin Laxenaire

licensing.notes: MIT verified via GitHub API 2026-11-03 (★1827).

candidates.research_notes: Repo fetched (HTTP 200) with real file listing and docs structure; the CSS-Tricks article by the same author (fetched 200) documents the displacement slideshow technique. Library is well-maintained and framework-free.
candidates.otxyn_potential: High: the bridge between DOM and WebGL—the 'geometry mask transition' template could produce multiple library entries (rings, spheres, scroll-ramp masks).

candidates.name: Morphing Page Transition
candidates.description: Page transition where the intro screen slides up while an SVG path morphs into another path, producing a flowy liquid look between pages; anime.js powers the path morph and Charming handles letter effects. Paths must share the same point count for a smooth morph.
candidates.creator: Codrops (Manoela Ilic)
techniques: page translate-up reveal synchronized with morph

licensing.notes: Codrops playing-ground effect; licence not verified.

candidates.research_notes: Demo page fetched (HTTP 200); repo URL extracted from the article HTML. Small, clear codebase (anime.js) showing the canonical SVG-morph transition.
candidates.otxyn_potential: Medium-high: a foundational SVG morphotype; easy to parameterize (any two equal-point paths) for the morphix lane of the library.

candidates.name: Scroll-Based Layout Animations
candidates.description: Compilation of on-scroll layout transitions: sections stay pinned while scrolling and GSAP ScrollTrigger + Flip morph the layout from grid to fullscreen image, from irregular grid to stacked images with title, etc., via a class-based style switch.
candidates.creator: Codrops

licensing.notes: Codrops resource; licence not verified.

candidates.research_notes: Demo and repo both fetched HTTP 200; article excerpt confirms ScrollTrigger+Flip 'class switch' technique and inspiration by Framer University / VRTL WORLD.
candidates.otxyn_potential: High: 'scroll morphs layout' is a highly requested pattern and the class-switch trick means actual CSS layouts stay hand-editable.

candidates.name: Fullscreen Scrolling Slideshow
candidates.description: Fullscreen slideshow navigated by scroll (Observer plugin) where slides transition fullscreen and clicking a slide reveals content underneath it; includes a jump-to-slide menu and letter-scramble micro transitions for the cursor/close UI.
candidates.creator: Codrops

licensing.notes: Codrops resource; licence not verified.

candidates.research_notes: Repo fetched (HTTP 200, real page with code files); article URL from the same Codrops family fetched earlier in this session via codrops hub (article page content confirmed). Design based on Chan + Eayrs studio.
candidates.otxyn_potential: Medium-high: page-transition-by-scroll (no scrollbar) is its own subgenre; the Observer pattern generalizes to any gesture-jacked fullscreen transition.

candidates.name: Scroll Transitions WebGL (Phenomenon)
candidates.description: Minimal demo by Colin van Eenige showing a WebGL image-to-image transition driven by scroll, built on Phenomenon (three.js-based): scroll position maps directly to transition progress between rendered planes.
candidates.creator: Colin van Eenige

licensing.notes: README (seen in extraction) states free use in personal/commercial projects, no re-sale/redistribution as-is, visible credit required; no formal licence URL verified.

candidates.research_notes: README completely extracted (article link 'As-Is. Scroll Transitions WebGL' + demo + credits + licence paragraph all present). The cleanest, smallest scroll→WebGL-transition mapping found so far; ideal as reference implementation rather than dependency (Phenomenon itself is minimally maintained).
candidates.otxyn_potential: High: template for the 'scroll drives a WebGL page-plane transition' pattern; could be ported onto modern GSAP ScrollTrigger or native scroll listeners without losing the shader core.

candidates.name: Cinematic 3D Scroll Experiences (Codrops tutorial demos)
candidates.description: Demos for a tutorial on building smooth, immersive 3D scroll experiences with GSAP — three.js scenes choreographed to scroll progress, combining WebG environments with DOM content transitions.
candidates.creator: Joseph ASG

licensing.notes: Repo fetched; licence not inspected.

candidates.otxyn_potential: Medium: closer to a scene-engine than a curated pattern; valuable as a template for 'scroll transitions that swap whole WebGL environments'.

candidates.name: Animated Grid Previews
candidates.description: Template where scattered thumbnail images animate into a final grid layout when the 'explore' link is clicked, with slight parallax on the background images; once settled, the page becomes scrollable and content shows beneath.
candidates.creator: Codrops (Manoela Ilic)
techniques: nav category switching with unique per-grid layouts

licensing.notes: Codrops resource; licence not verified.

candidates.otxyn_potential: High: 'scatter → settle grid' is a signature editorial opener and doubles as a gallery transition.

candidates.name: Ambient Canvas Backgrounds
candidates.description: Five ambient webpage background animations built in vanilla ES6 with the Canvas API (three use a Simplex noise library): flowing particle fields, wind lines and curves drawn offscreen then composited to the onscreen canvas, deliberately non-distracting.
candidates.creator: Sean Free (Codrops)
techniques: offscreen buffer canvas + filtered composite to screen
typed-array particle properties instead of objects

licensing.notes: Codrops resource; licence not verified.

candidates.otxyn_potential: High: quintessential generative background tier — calm, CPU-light, zero dependencies; directly portable and easily themeable via palette arrays.

candidates.name: Wave.js
candidates.description: GPU-accelerated animated sine-wave background library (~11 kB, zero dependencies, MIT): batched draw-call wave fields with theme presets (liquid metal, frosted glass, split fill), automatic WebGL2→Canvas2D→CSS-gradient fallback chain, and React + vanilla APIs.
candidates.creator: redesigner (@redesigner/wave.js)

licensing.notes: MIT licence stated on the site (observed in fetched content); GitHub URL not verified so licence_url left empty.

candidates.research_notes: Site fetched (HTTP 200) with the full parameter list and architecture notes visible; live configurable preview on the page itself. Modern, packaged, and explicitly promotes per-frame GPU writes — an unusual, production-ready wave implementation.
candidates.otxyn_potential: High: closest thing to a drop-in, dependency-free wave background with graceful degradation; ideal library entry 'as-is' or as a shader reference.

candidates.name: Terax Line Waves (OGL)
candidates.description: React component rendering concentric line-wave field with OGL: inner/outer line counts, warp intensity, rotation and edge fade sum into a colour-cycling 2D wave background on a fullscreen triangle.
candidates.creator: crynta
techniques: concentric sin/cos line bands from vertex shader

licensing.notes: File URL fetched via extraction showing real source; repo licence file not inspected.

candidates.otxyn_potential: High as a code template: this is exactly what the curated library wants — one file, one effect, named parameters; trivially converted to vanilla.

candidates.name: Stripe WebGL Effect (ribbon recreation)
candidates.description: WebGL2 recreation study of the Stripe-style animated folded-ribbon hero: densely subdivided plane folded in geometry space with procedural twist, simplex noise displacement, shader-based fibre lines and depth-based focal effects.
candidates.creator: AGE-T
techniques: 400×400-style dense plane with pre-fold geometry and X-section reversal
explicit WebGL2 state management per pass

candidates.otxyn_potential: Medium-high: the ribbon family is otherwise under-served; this documents the necessary fold+noise geometry approach in enough detail to rebuild generically.

candidates.name: Block Reveal Effects
candidates.description: Two-family set of content reveal effects: a decorative block is drawn, grows, then shrinks away to uncover the content underneath — seed/block and half-page/full-page demo variants, some with CSS clip-path animation, plus uncovered-piece variations on scroll.
candidates.creator: Codrops (Manoela Ilic)

licensing.notes: Codrops resource; licence not verified.

candidates.name: Background Shift Animation with CSS Blend Modes
candidates.description: Effect remake of the Alef Estate site: on scroll the whole viewport transitions to a contrasting (black) background via a slice animation, with the custom cursor tied to the swap through mix-blend-mode tricks.
candidates.creator: Codrops (Manoela Ilic)
techniques: slice-wise background invert driven by scroll timeline

candidates.otxyn_potential: High: 'theme-invert wipe on scroll' is a current trend (blend-mode content reveals); very few deps so readily reusable.

candidates.name: Mesh Gradient Generator (gradients.sh)
candidates.description: Browser studio for generating live animated mesh gradients: 2–6 softly-shaded colour fields blended in OKLab by a shader, drifting on closed circular loops so motion is seamless and MP4 exports loop exactly; responds to pointer and scroll; exports code embeds and PNG/MP4.
candidates.creator: gradients.sh
techniques: per-colour light fields blended in OKLab avoiding perceptual mud
closed circular path drift for lossless looping

licensing.notes: Unknown for the shader core; code export requires a free account. Commercial-friendly engine but no licence text on the inspected page.

candidates.research_notes: Page fetched (HTTP 200); the tool copy itself enumerates the whole technical approach (OKLab, circular drift, loops). The most complete animated mesh-gradient implementation found; free tier includes 1080p60 MP4 loop export.
candidates.otxyn_potential: Very high: the generated loops/components are directly embeddable as library 'assets', and the parameter list effectively designs the API for any in-house mesh-gradient shader we write.

candidates.name: Remotion Light Leaks
candidates.description: Shader module generating organic light-leak transition/overlay effects: warm yellow-orange fractal-noise patterns evolve in and retract out (reveal + erase threshold ramps), with seed, hueShift and progress uniforms — designed as a screen-blend layer for video.
candidates.creator: Remotion team

licensing.notes: Remotion's repository licences are custom/mixed; candidate ships inside Remotion whose terms differ by company size. Licence NOT verified — treat code as reference-only unless the Remotion terms are reviewed.

candidates.research_notes: Extraction returned actual GLSL source: computePattern() with iterative cos-domain warp, smoothstep threshold ramps for evolve/retract, yellow→orange mix by pattern value. The only solid ambient-light-transition shader found this session; designed for video but technique is directly web-portable.
candidates.otxyn_potential: High: the shader isolates cleanly to a 'light-leak page/screen transition' DOM overlay; seeds+progress make it deterministic and loop-friendly.
